title: A Matched-Budget Audit Framework for Recaptioned Image-Text Supervision Distributions
topic: Data-centric AI->Data-centric AI methods and tools
claim: Every automated annotator carries bias; the chosen policy determines which biases enter the data, shown by examples and diagnostics.
layout: 2 panels: left text examples with image, right dual-axis bar-line chart
description: The figure has two panels. Panel (a), "Policy sets the caption register", puts a snowy winter-path photo at upper left. Beside it are two rounded boxes: a purple "Long-form describe" box and a blue "Broad-frame template" box. Each box holds caption snippets with highlighted frame prefixes such as "This image displays:" and "There are". A legend marks the highlight as a describe-style frame. A green callout reads "Every captioning policy injects bias; the policy decides which biases enter the corpus." Below it, a green box labeled "Ours (prompt-aligned)" shows a dense caption with multicolor span highlights. Panel (b), "Prompt-pool diagnostics", is a dual-axis chart for four corpora: DataComp, LAION-pop, PD12M and Danbooru. Blue (Ours) and orange (Ref) bars show prompt-mass support. Lines with markers show n-gram JSD, and Ours is generally better.
caption: VLM bias is inevitable; policy decides which biases survive. Left:\protect\footnotemark{} describe-style frame prefix concentration drops on the released surface. Right: averaged across 7 prompt pools per cross-corpus pair, Ours raises prompt-mass support on every pair and lowers $n$-gram Jensen-Shannon Divergence (JSD) against the pool distribution on DataComp, PD12M, and Danbooru, with the length-matched LAION-pop pair within $0.01$; bars on the left axis report support, markers on the right axis report JSD; definitions are in Section [ref].
abstract: Recaptioned image-text corpora are now standard for text-to-image (T2I) training, with vision--language model (VLM) captioners replacing sparse alt-text by dense descriptions. A recaptioned corpus is a supervision distribution induced by a documented captioning policy ($Ï$), captioner ($V_c$), and source corpus ($C$). Length-correlated proxies miss caption-register artifacts and downstream T2I benchmarks entangle the corpus with training choices, so this distribution is hard to audit at corpus scale. We introduce a reusable matched-budget audit framework for recaptioned supervision distributions $D_{Ï,V_c,C}$: at a fixed text budget of $B = 64$ it reports a five-axis profile spanning prompt-side coverage, image-conditioned faithfulness, and caption-surface health, with claimed controllable basic units (CBU) as the common claim unit. We instantiate the framework on seven paired comparisons over five public source corpora. Across the four cross-corpus pairs, the released surface raises supported CBU per caption by $+3.39$ to $+6.36$ under both Qwen and Gemma Judges, and on CC12M the same framework exposes a long-vs-dense frontier that is consistent across both judges and four budgets. We release the audited multi-source recap corpus ($\approx$ 490M) together with the audit-artifact bundle.
